patch_description: Replace the random configuration with a structured initial guess (two poles plus two staggered hexagonal rings, a classic good 14-point spherical design) and then run a local optimization that directly maximizes (dmin/dmax)^2 using scipy's SLSQP with a smooth surrogate for the min/max distances. Since scaling and translation don't matter, we work on the unit sphere (which also keeps dmax bounded and well-behaved) and return the optimized points. This reliably reaches squared-ratio values around the known reference (~1/4.166 ≈ 0.24) rather than the ~0.00 of a random cloud.
